title.narrative: Fiscal Management Efficiency Project (formerly Fiscal Management Reform Program II)

description.narrative: The project aims to ensure greater sustainability of public investments in Sri Lanka, particularly in the less developed regions, through more effective public resource management. It seeks to do so by enhancing the fiscal space (i.e., availability of greater resources) as a result of bringing about improved tax administration and compliance as well as more efficient public financial management. This will be largely attained through establishment of two management information system- one related to revenue and the other to expenditure management.

Output: More capable public resource managers Indicator: At least 50% of the trained technical staff members are retained for the project period (2009 baseline: no officers trained yet on RAMIS and ITMIS) Achievement: 0

Output: More capable public resource managers Indicator: Basic computerized training programs for up to 1,500 officials at tax offices and spending units (2009 baseline: no training program in place) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Basic computerized training programs have been conducted for 200 officials for ITMIS and 800 more officials are planned to be trained by end of May 2017. Approximately 600 users have been trained in RAMIS.

Output: More capable public resource managers Indicator: Revenue and treasury training programs for up to 2,000 users of RAMIS and ITMIS (2009 baseline: no program yet; RAMIS and ITMIS not yet in place) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: For ITMIS, the training programs were conducted for MoF for Phases 1, 2 and 3. Output: More accountable revenue management Indicator: The number of tax filers to increase by at least 15% (2009 baseline: approximately 150,000 tax filers) Achievement: 168941 Progress/Status: The number of tax filers have doubled and currently there are 318,941 tax filers. Output: More accountable revenue management Indicator: Computerized risk-based selection of audit files to be introduced (2009 baseline: manual selection of files for audit) Achievement: N Progress/Status: RAMIS has an audit module under which audit rules are automated and it has several audit criteria configurable with thresholds. IRD is planning to clear all the backlog of pending assessment and post that use this module for risk-based selection of audit files.

Output: More accountable revenue management Indicator: Electronic filing of tax returns to be introduced (2009 baseline: no e-filing facility) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The e-filing of tax returns was introduced in March 2016 for the following taxes: CIT, PAYE, NBT, SVAT, VAT and WHT Data Source: DIR departmental report Baseline year: 2009 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2009 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: More accountable revenue management Indicator: RAMIS fully operational (2009 baseline: RAMIS not in place) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: RAMIS was implemented in a phased manner. Phase 1, comprising of CIT, PAYE, NBT, SVAT, VAT, WHT, went live in December 2016, while Phase 2 and VAT FS was made fully functional within 2017. However, with the recent amendments to the Inland Revenue Act, several areas in phases 1 and 2 of RAMIS are being currently revised, which will be completed by the end of 2019. Data Source: Budget speeches, budget circulars, and supplementary budgets Baseline year: 2009 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2009 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Each taxpayer may be linked to multiple tax types through this unique no to provide a consolidated view of the taxpayer. The TIN number is of 9 digits which can be increased to 12 digits.
